## Security verdict: BLOCK

PR #170, exact head `bfe2301bdbf6cc62d7f720270fabc11a8fcc17df`.

Reviewed the prune-tooling diff and its directly dependent process/seat/removal guards. Partial or failed cwd observation can authorize removal of a clean worktree that still has a process using it.

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| 1 | 🟡 MEDIUM | harness/scripts/pr-freeze.ts | 576-601 | Incomplete process-cwd enumeration fails open and can remove an occupied worktree | 9/10 |

### S170-001: observation failure is treated as absence

The macOS branch accepts nonempty `lsof` output even when the command reports an error. Nonempty output containing no cwd records becomes an empty process list. The Linux branch suppresses every `/proc/<pid>/cwd` read error, including permission/observation failures rather than only processes demonstrably gone.

With an eligible clean worktree and an unregistered process using it, unreadable or omitted cwd evidence yields no occupancy veto (`pr-freeze.ts:653-662`), and the script invokes removal (`664-665`). Other readable processes can make the overall observation look nonempty while the relevant occupant is missing. `git worktree remove` dirty/locked checks do not establish that no process occupies a clean checkout or protect its ignored contents.

The test fixture explicitly accepts exit-code-1 output accompanied by `denied` (`harness/scripts/pr-freeze.test.ts:581-591`). This is a source-derived failure path, not a local pruning experiment.

Refuse before any removal when enumeration is unsuccessful, incomplete or malformed. On Linux, distinguish confirmed process exit from permission/observation failure; uncertainty must not authorize deletion.

### Other scope and safety evidence

- Actual policy includes MERGED, CLOSED, **and OPEN with a superseded head** (`pr-freeze.ts:549-555`), not just completed PRs.
- Candidates come from registered Git worktrees and must have the anchored `review-<digits>-<seven lowercase hex>` basename, detached HEAD and matching SHA prefix (`pr-freeze.ts:216-230,510-516,543-546,620`). This establishes name/HEAD agreement, not historical PR-commit membership.
- Status errors, tracked/untracked changes, reported seat folders and observed process cwds veto removal. Active and idle seats remain represented; there is no activity-only filter.
- Removal uses discrete argv and `git worktree remove` without `--force`, with no recursive-shell deletion fallback (`pr-freeze.ts:636-675,710-717`). No demonstrated shell/option-injection path was identified.
- Failed realpath resolution falls back to the original path, and process-cwd strings are not canonicalized (`pr-freeze.ts:607-612,653-655`). This review does not establish an adversarial symlink/rogue-worktree-metadata guarantee; it is not reported as a separate demonstrated exploit.
- Changed fixtures use synthetic paths; no new C19/C21 disclosure was identified.

### Proof

GitHub metadata and the independent remote pull ref agree on the full reviewed SHA; GitHub reports CLEAN. CI run `42429696026` and Delivers run `42429695920` both identify this SHA and success. Green CI does not establish fail-closed enumeration: the cited fixture accepts the unsafe result.

No local tests, builds, process probes, prune execution, worktree removals, credential reads or mutations were performed.
